articles.body:
I'm sure this has been answered before, but I couldn't find any obvious hits when searching.

King Arthur's hero power says: "If your opponent cancels the effects on your attack card, the BOOST is discarded without effect."

Is discarding the BOOST [b]instead of[/b] or [b]in addition to[/b] canceling the attack card's effects?

There was some contention over this in our first game. :whistle:

articles.body:
The most fair thing we have thought is for Arthur and his opponent to place their attack and defense card face down as normal. After the defender has committed to their defense card but neither has revealed what they're playing, Arthur can then place his boost card face down.

We felt that if Arthur puts down his initial attack card and the card he wants to boost with, it makes it way too easy for him to get fainted; especially because the defender could wait until he puts his two cards face down on the table and then play feint.
We

We also play more free for all at three and four player matches than one on one, so Arthur could be fainted up to nine times in a game.  We played a one on one tournament yesterday and even with the way we play Arthur, he still didn't win, so while this method didn't get him a win, it still feels like a fair way to rule how you play it.

articles.body: I personally don't seem to play Arthur much; every game we draw labeled cards to randomize who we play. Boosting every attack, how often do you wind up milling yourself or running out of cards in hand leaving yourself vulnerable?  Next time I play him one on one I may try that, but it might be rough in three and four player matches, especially since politics of the game tend to be as two players go down in health and one player has more, that higher health person tends to get ganged up on a bit.

articles.body:
[q="Hobomagic"]I personally don't seem to play Arthur much; every game we draw labeled cards to randomize who we play. Boosting every attack, how often do you wind up milling yourself or running out of cards in hand leaving yourself vulnerable?  Next time I play him one on one I may try that, but it might be rough in three and four player matches, especially since politics of the game tend to be as two players go down in health and one player has more, that higher health person tends to get ganged up on a bit. [/q]

In a 3 or 4 person game the dynamic might be a bit different with Arthur, I haven't tried him in one like that but I imagine the strategy might be different. I've heard in team play 2v2 matches he can be pretty good but I haven't played him that way yet. 

As far as 1v1 goes, I find the most effective way to play with him is by boosting frequently. Yes, you will burn through cards that way but it makes it really tough for the opponent to know when to use a feint and it eats their health away quickly because almost every attack does damage. Let me give you a few examples of some ways I use his boost that I find make him most efficient. I've played him against Sherlock this way and absolutely blew out Sherlock, had 12 health for KA left and 7 for Merlin left. 

- Swift Strike has an attack value of 3 and boost value of two. If I need to get away from someone I will use it without boosting but if I have some decent attack cards in my hand, like Skirmish (4 attack), then I will use Swift strike to boost. That gives an attack value of 6 and if not feinted will usually do 2-3 damage. 
- Skirmish and Aid of Morgana are worth 4 attack. Played by itself vs a 3 defense card it does just 1 damage. Boost it with something like regroup (1 attack) and you get 2 damage. If you play regroup by itself as an attack card you most likely won't deal any damage and the only benefit you get is drawing a card. Playing it with Skirmish makes regroup useful by dealing extra damage and it may draw a feint out from your opponent. A boost with Noble Sacrifice gives Skirmish or Aid of Morgana up to 7 attack. 
- Excalibur should ALWAYS be boosted with noble sacrifice for a max of 9 attack. If you get to use Excalibur 2x try to boost it the second time with Noble Sacrifice as well. That gives you two attacks of 9 damage. If feinted you would deal a total of 8 damage from both attacks and if no feint is used for either of them you're going to be dealing 10-12 damage total from both attacks. If you only get Excalibur once then save the other two noble sacrifice cards to use with Noble Sacrifice (preferred, max of 8 damage) or Skirmish (max of 7 damage). 
- Momentous shift I always try to use after some movement has taken place to get the attack value of 5 with it. Then boost it with a Noble Sacrifice and it is worth a max of 8 damage. Notice how these options give you attacks that can range anywhere from 6 to 9 depending on the base card and boost card used. That IMO is a ton of versatility and makes it so you have more than "just excalibur" to do serious damage with. Let's say you only get Excalibur once and then you boost Momentous shift 2x with the other 2 noble sacrifice cards, that gives you attack of 9, 8 and 8. If you attack frequently with boosting the changes of all 3 attacks being feinted are pretty slim. If they do feint all 3 you still deal 4, 3 and 3 damage for a total of 10 damage. If they don't feint you deal 6, 5 and 5 damage (if 3 defense is used) or 5, 4 and 4 damage (if 4 defense is used). 
- Save your weaker cards that are worth 2-3 defense and use them for defending as KA. Since he has higher health than most characters and Merlin can sometimes step in and take some damage (with Bewilderment) it gives him flexibility to defend with weaker cards and use the stronger ones for attacking. Also using Holy Grail at a key moment can really hurt your opponent end of game and be a turning point. An example is when I played Robin, he moved in and used his strongest attack to try to finish me off. I played Holy Grail and it brought my health back up to 8 and essentially made his 5 attack card a waste and was the shift in the match. 
- I like to use most of my Divine Intervention cards either for defensive purposes or for boosting depending on my hand and what I need more at the time. 
- Keep Merlin alive as long as possible since he is very important for success, especially the scheme cards he has like Restless Spirits which does 2 damage AND lets you draw cards if you use it to defeat someone. His ranged attack is great for chasing enemies down and his "bewilderment" cards can be useful at key moments.

articles.body:
[q="ClumsySpirit"][q="vtyler98"]Let's say you only get Excalibur once and then you boost Momentous shift 2x with the other 2 noble sacrifice cards, that gives you attack of 9, 8 and 8. If you attack frequently with boosting the changes of all 3 attacks being feinted are pretty slim. If they do feint all 3 you still deal 4, 3 and 3 damage for a total of 10 damage. If they don't feint you deal 6, 5 and 5 damage (if 3 defense is used) or 5, 4 and 4 damage (if 4 defense is used).[/q]

I don't believe your math here is correct. If momentous shift is feinted, not only will the boost be discarded, but also momentous shift's effect will be canceled, resulting in only 1 damage to your opponent. That's not to say that you shouldn't boost momentous shift, but be aware that this is a high-risk/high-reward strategy.

Otherwise, excellent post. Definitely some ideas there that I'll have to try out. I tend to think of Skirmish as a primarily defensive card, but I think you've convinced me that I should be attacking with it.[/q]

Yeah the assumption is the attack is 8 if no feint is utilized. Otherwise the attack value is 3. What I find is that by boosting frequently it draws out feints and overwhelms your opponent. Here’s another way I look at it visually, which really helps me. 

Here are the ideal combinations that deal 6+ attack. Top row is 9 attack, next row is max of 8, then 7, then 6 for the bottom row. This gives KA a total of 7 possible attacks that are valued at 6+ attack if not feinted. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/MI5cARq.jpg[/img]

Obviously in a match one wouldn’t utilize all 7 of these combinations, I find I usually use 4-5 of them before my opponent is defeated, but it gives an idea of the attack potential KA has. Outside of Bigfoot and invisible man as feint anomalies, every other character has 3 cards to feint with. Even in a worst case scenario where Excalibur is used once/feinted and both momentous shifts are feinted as well, you will have dealt 6 total damage and drawn out all 3 feints. This still leaves you with 1 max of 7 boosted attack and 3 additional 6 boosted attacks that can’t be feinted. That’s some serious firepower to deal with and I find that usually when I boost often that at least one or two of my boosted momentous shifts or boosted Excalibur will get through. This keeps the opponent on edge and they really have to choose when to deploy feint if you boost most or all of KA’s attacks. I remember Justin also mentioned a key to success is to use the boost frequently and this path imo is what maximizes his boost potential. 

Yeah Skirmish can be boosted up to 6 or 7 attack depending on what boost card is used. I sometimes will even boost it with a regroup to make skirmish worth a max of 5 attack. I typically use my weaker defense cards like feint, regroup, and divine intervention (if not needed in combat) to defend with. I find by attacking and boosting aggressively it usually puts opponents on the run, especially if a big 8 or 9 attack is landed. This then allows Arthur to fill his hand back up and Merlin can be used at range to snipe if needed. 

The biggest weakness for KA is against characters like Bigfoot who has basically 5 feint type cards and Medusa who is ranged and has discard text in some of her cards. Curious to see if any of these tips help others in playing KA!

articles.body:
Last post to add to this, but here is why I think the benefits of boosting are key and I'll give a few scenarios of why. 

Let's say you have skirmish and swift strike and decide to attack with both of those cards separately, without boosting. Let's assume for both cards the opponent plays a base 3 defense card, one of the most common in the game. The skirmish is 4 vs 3 and does 1 damage, the swift strike is 3 vs 3 and does 0 damage. [b]You played 2 cards to deal 1 damage. [/b]

Now let's look at the exact same scenario but boosted. The Skirmish is 4 and swift strike adds +2 attack. This gives a total attack of 6. Assuming the opponent played the same 3 defense card [b]you deal 3 damage with 2 cards and if feinted it would deal 2 damage.[/b] Yes you lose out on the card effects but the trade off is you dealt more damage to your opponent. 

Another scenario, let's say you play momentous shift with the movement action taking effect (5 value) and then boost it with a regroup, valued at only 1. This gives a total attack of 6 if not feinted and against a common 3 defense card does 3 damage. Now let's say you play regroup and momentous shift separately. Regroup is valued at only 1 so no damage is done and momentous shift at 5 would do 2 damage vs a 3 defense card. The difference in boosting is you dealt 1 extra damage from a card that rarely ever does damage (regroup) but lost the card effect of drawing a card. 

This is why IMO boosting aggressively with Arthur is the way to go. It forces your opponents to pick and choose when to use their feints (making it easier to land a big blow via boosted Excalibur or something else) while also making attacks more effective. It can put your opponent on the run if big damage is dealt allowing you to fill your hand up as well and snipe with Merlin. I find it is important to make sure you have adequate defense cards in your hand after boosting to defend back with, especially one like feint or divine intervention that can let you move away from your opponent if you are in a bad spot. I like to save my divine intervention cards for just that purpose and try not to use them for attacking or boosting unless I'm going for a killing blow. 

One of my favorite tactics to use if I am adjacent to my opponent to start the turn (and have the hand to allow it) is to attempt two big heavy hitting attacks. For the first one I might do Excalibur boosted up to 9 and for the second something like Skirmish boosted to 6 or 7 attack. This can allow a big first hit (even if feint is used) and then the second boosted attack can deal some big damage as well while also allowing you to retreat some (assuming no feint). I've done this before and dealt 10 damage in one turn like that which sends most opponents into a bit of a panic. The other benefit of boosting attacks as mentioned in the scenarios mentioned above is that it is often difficult to attack your opponent 2x in one turn. I find I typically have to maneuver first to get in range and then attack. Not only do you deal more damage by boosting but it's like getting 2 attacks in with 1 action. Anyways just some thoughts of mine and why I love playing with KA, he's so much fun.

Making being bullied more tolerable by giving you things you can bully yourself.

So you want to boost all the time, but you don't want an empty hand. Not sure how that works.[/q]

I'm not sure how you or your opponents typically play, but I never have issues with an empty hand when playing as King Arthur and boosting attacks frequently. I have beaten Robin with King Arthur and didn't find him that hard to be honest. It was a very close game but the holy grail was the turning point near the end and that was with one of my Excalibur attacks being feinted away. In the end the constant boosted attacks of KA were just too much for Robin Hood and simply overwhelmed him. Also, in Cobble & Fog many consider Sherlock the strongest character (perhaps on par with bigfoot/medusa) and I obliterated him with KA, it wasn't even close.  I get it, you feel like KA is broken and needs to be fixed but I don't see that at all and I don't see any need for the developers to "fix" him because I don't consider him broken. I feel like he is one of the harder characters to use effectively but once you figure out the nuances of what makes him work well he is very good, on par with Sinbad, Robin, Alice or Bruce Lee IMO. I never have once felt I needed a perfect deck and bad luck for my opponent to win with him. 

Medusa and Bigfoot are tough matchups for KA simply due to the way their deck and cards work (5 feints for bigfoot and discard text for Medusa + she is ranged) but they are still winnable and even more rewarding when you pull it off. Sure Bigfoot and Medusa are the two stronger characters in the game because of how straightforward their abilities and attacks are but they are beatable by any character, I never go into a match against them thinking "man I don't have a chance unless I get super lucky." I have all the expansions and typically play over a dozen times a week, sometimes more when time allows, and have never found a single character that gives me the feeling of being a "rock paper scissors" luck based game.  Although they are harder matchups for KA they are still winnable even if you get a bad hand or things don't go "perfectly." As more characters and abilities are introduced you have to realize there are simply going to be some matches where one character may be at a bit of a disadvantage due to how their cards or special ability is designed (and thematically this would make sense also). 

And yes, with King Arthur you can boost attacks frequently without running out of cards. King Arthur and Merlin have cards that allow him to draw additional cards and he also has some cards that allow him to move away after combat (if not feinted). Before I ever played a single match with King Arthur I spent several days researching him, looking at his cards, thinking of various strategies and outcomes, reading the reports of others, doing the math on what would be most efficient, etc. and what I've outlined above works VERY well for me and is a result of all the time I spent learning his character. I do this research with every character btw but especially KA since there were so many threads about him. I can beat any character with him without needing the "stars to align."

articles.body:
[q="ClumsySpirit"][q="Saduhem"]You literally can't win unless your deck is stacked perfectly and you opponent's is cursed. A game shouldn't be balanced with "Never play with X against W, Y, or Z". Outcome being decided at hero selection removes the point of playing at all, and it becomes a pretty version of Rock, Paper, Scissors. Except that, in Rocks, Paper, Scissors, there's only 1 possible combination that will make you lose.

No 1v1 game is perfectly balanced, but neither have I EVER played one that had such skewed matchups. I really, really can't come up with anything that's more one-sided. What's worse is the complete absence of attempts to address it. I guess extending the roster to things you can actually play against and ignoring the rest is one way to do it. Making being bullied more tolerable by giving you things you can bully yourself.[/q]

I'm still uncertain about exactly how well-balanced Unmatched is, but what you have described is simply innacurate. King Arthur is fully capable of beating every other character (without a stacked deck or cursed opponent), and while, yes, certain matchups are going to be harder than others, this game is nowhere close to Rock, Paper, Scissors.[/q]

I've played a good bit of matches with all of the expansions and it is very well balanced. To me the way I consider it balanced or not is can I take one character and beat any other hero of my choice and not feel like I need a perfect deck to do so? There's not a single character that I would classify like that in the series thus far, I can take King Arthur and feel like I can beat anyone including Medusa or Bigfoot and I can take the raptors and feel like I can beat anyone else out there. Obviously some matches you're going to get a bad hand, and for a character like Bruce Lee that relies on hand management and building up a combo, that can make things a bit tougher. At the same time the tension of never knowing when Lee will unleash a big combo, when KA will do a boosted Excalibur, the Raptors will move in for a big attack, when Hyde might unleash a devasting blow with "Forever Hyde" or Dracula with Beastform I find the tension and strategies diverse, exciting, and fun each time I play. It's my #1 go to game right now and probably will be for some time.
